prompt:
Professional fashion photograph, demi-statue demi statue portrait, irregular asymmetric-panelled multi-material body, every seam physically stepped, no bare skin below the collarbones. ONE woman, angled 45 degrees toward the camera, framed so her whole sculpted form is visible from the top of her head down to two individually finished thigh tips a little further below the middle of her thighs, just above where the knee would be, her face in natural scale with her body — never an oversized close-up crop of just the face. Where her form comes to an end, it is because the sculpture itself ends there, not because a camera frame happens to cut her off.

Subject: A real photograph of a strikingly beautiful adult Korean woman in girl-crush makeup — fair ivory skin, sharply angled thin brows, a razor-sharp winged cat-eye liner extending far past the outer corner, deep brown-black eyeshadow, long lashes, large eyes with bright real catchlights, strongly sculpted contour, a deep wine-red matte lip, long sleek black hair, a cold, commanding gaze. Her whole face, ears and neck are real living flesh with real pores and fine skin grain, real living eyes with bright catchlights and genuine depth, individual hair strands catching the light — a photograph of a real face, not an illustration, not a render, not cel-shaded. On each ear a big black-steel hoop and a thick bar.

Physique: A colossal heavy chest wider than her shoulders, a waistline that still pulls in sharply, then an enormous belly and colossal wide hips flaring out again, her body in irregular black-bordered panels, demi-statue

Boundary: a single straight, flat line runs around the base of the neck and across both collarbones, never jagged, never zigzag — real skin above, material immediately below, no skin anywhere lower. At that line, the material's edge rises in a small raised step, casting a crisp shadow. Below this line, there is no bare skin anywhere on her body below this line — every part, without exception, is one of the materials described.

Her whole body below the collarbones is divided into four irregular rectangular panels of different sizes, separated by thick matte-black bands: large panel (left arm, upper-left chest) solid transparent golden-yellow citrine crystal crystal; narrow panel (right arm) carved vivid sky-blue turquoise with dark matrix veining, completely opaque; small square panel (belly centre) a glass vessel of clear rose-pink water with drifting rose petals; large panel (hips and both legs) carved dark wenge wood with fine gold-tan pinstripes, completely opaque. At every seam where two pieces meet, one edge rises very slightly above its neighbour, casting a thin, crisp shadow — proving each piece is a truly separate object, not a flat pattern painted on one surface. A little further below the middle of her thighs, just above where the knee would be, her left thigh seals shut into its own small, smooth, rounded, closed tip (the same rose-pink vessel panel); her right thigh rounds off into its own small, smooth, satin-polished carved tip (the same wenge wood panel).

Setting: a huge backdrop behind her washed with two coloured lights from behind — a soft cream white on one side and a deep crimson red on the other, blending into a smooth gradient in the middle, and a glossy dark floor beneath her.

Pose: standing tall, her left hand resting on her flared hip, her right arm held clear of her body, the hand relaxed at hip height, both hands well away from her face, head tilted slightly toward the camera.

Lighting: two large softboxes rake across her body from either side, so white light glances off one side and red light glances off the other, catching a crisp glint along every stepped seam. A soft frontal light falls on her face and ears only. shot on a Hasselblad X2D with an 85mm lens, shallow depth of field. 2:3 vertical 8K portrait.
